rationale: C18 is a near-verbatim template for the child: both identify a named federal official who will become subject to compulsory retirement under the same Civil Service Retirement Act unless exempted by Executive order, then state the same public-interest justification and transition to the operative provision. C08 uses substantially the same machinery with modestly different phrasing, while C11 preserves only the public-interest recital and transition.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS Paul A. Walker, a member of the Federal Communications Commission, will, during the month of January 1951, become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas Eugene Black, Judge, Tax Court of the United States, will, during the month of July 1949, become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.explanation: The child reproduces the distinctive retirement predicate almost verbatim, substituting the official, office, and date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below: NOW, THEREFORE
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below: NOW, THEREFORE
shared_material.explanation: The justification and transition are verbatim, completing the same two-recital drafting sequence.
